finding.title: Unprotected diagnostic parsing can preempt audit-denial result precedence
finding.evidence: Line 446 reads and JSON-parses every audit log line before checking marker or exit78 at 448-456. Line 459 similarly parses boundary lines before result construction. Partial/unreadable diagnostic data from the explicitly supported persistence-failure/fail-stop path can raise and prevent result.json from carrying INFRA_BLOCKED_AUDIT_DENIAL. Later child-outcome/ready reads are also unprotected auxiliary decoding.
finding.impact: R397 requires every marker, exit78 or denial row to force the blocked classification even when persistence is incomplete. Cleanup happens first and the child still stops, but a partial audit record can defeat the required result and causal-verdict classification. This is reporting failure, not product continuation or observed network escape.
finding.recommendation: Route through actual Astra. Establish denial from marker existence/exit78 before fallible decoding, preserve raw diagnostic bytes, record read/decode/type errors and valid rows, and prevent auxiliary artifact parsing from masking the known denial. No repair or test was performed by reviewer.

previous_child_stop_defect: R396-I1 resolved statically in R397; no continuation regression claimed.
